children: Indian stocks are likely to open on a flat to negative note on Thursday, amid cautious sentiment in the market. Gift Nifty at 25,240 signals a flattish opening for Nifty. After the announcement that US inflation rose sharply, the focus shifts to India’s number.

According to Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, Indian equity markets are likely to open on a steady note, with investors keeping a close watch on the October CPI inflation data scheduled for release later today. “This remains the key domestic catalyst, particularly after the recent acceleration in inflation and the RBI’s shift towards a calibrated tightening stance following its October rate hike. A higher-than-expected October print could reinforce concerns over further monetary tightening, while a softer reading may offer some relief to market sentiment,” he added.

Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, said lower crude oil prices continue to provide a supportive backdrop, but the US 10-year Treasury yield hovering near 4.99%, coupled with the market’s extended rally, may restrict an immediate upside.

“Brent crude trading near $92 a barrel reflects growing expectations of a de-escalation in US–Iran tensions and improving energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The decline offers some relief to India’s macroeconomic outlook and corporate earnings by easing oil-related pressures. However, the benefits are likely to prove more meaningful if lower prices are sustained, rather than reversed by renewed geopolitical tensions,” he said.

Global markets recovered overnight, led by technology shares. However, hotter-than-expected US inflation has strengthened expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase. If US Treasury yields remain near or above 5%, foreign investors may adopt a more selective approach towards Indian equities, despite the sharp retreat in crude oil prices, he further said.

Angel One, in a technical outlook said,the new Samvat 2083 began on a positive note, although buyers failed to sustain the higher levels following a gap-up opening. After a mid-week holiday, the gap-up trend continued; however, this time, sellers managed to gain the upper hand. Prices came under sustained selling pressure shortly after the opening bell, eventually erasing the entire opening gap and dragging the index lower.

“Following a sharp 3000-point rally over the past two weeks, which has resulted in a complete retracement of more than 100% of the preceding downswing, bulls appear to have taken firm control of the frontline index, NIFTY. The underlying strength is also evident in the equally impressive recovery witnessed across its constituent stocks, reflecting broad-based buying interest. That said, the sharp and relentless upmove has pushed nearly all technical and market-breadth indicators into overbought territory, suggesting that the rally may be approaching a short-term point of exhaustion,” it said.

Going forward, while the underlying trend remains bullish, the possibility of a short-term consolidation or corrective decline cannot be ruled out, it cautioned. Consequently, participants would be well advised to avoid chasing the ongoing momentum and instead consider initiating fresh long positions on dips towards well-defined support zones, where the risk-reward proposition is more favourable.

title: Flattish opening seen for Indian stocks; markets eye release of inflation data
